text:
samir: Proposal: start an 'adaptive GPU portfolio' for our spot pools. Instead of a fixed instance-type mix, maintain a scored shortlist per AZ and pick the top N each allocation cycle. Goals: lower cost, smoother eviction surface, and more predictable perf for critical models.

maria: +1. How do we compute the score? price + historical preempt rate + perf variance + network/PCIe topology?

kevin: Add memory footprint and NUMA/PCIe locality as penalties. Multi-instance-pack fragmentation is a real cost.

olivia: Can we quantify 99p latency impact vs cost savings? want an easy simulator before we flip anything in prod.

samir: Rough scoring proto:
```json
{"score_weights": {"price": 0.4, "preempt_rate": 0.3, "latency_var": 0.2, "pci_topology": 0.1}}
```
Also need per-model perf profiles (seq-len dist, batch sensitivity) so we can weight latency_var by workload mix.

jyoti: Note: network egress/region constraints matter for customer data zones. If we pick an instance type in a neighboring AZ/region to avoid preemptions, we must account for cross-AZ egress and replication lag.

infra-bot: [alert] us-west-2: preemption spike on p4-equivalents in last 24h (+22% compared to baseline).

kevin: Diversification helps when preemptions correlate by family. But hetero pools increase small-batch fragmentation -> higher 99p for low-latency routes. We need metrics for "pack fragmentation" and per-route tail latency.

samir: Action items: (1) build 2-week sim-run using the proto weights, (2) generate perf profiles for top-10 models, (3) deploy a tiny canary in staging for us-west-2 with adaptive selection + automatic fallback to dedicated pools. Volunteers?

maria: I'll own the sim + pulling historical interruption rates per SKU from billing logs.

olivia: I'll do the staging canary and define rollback criteria (max 99p latency delta, error budget safety).

kevin: I'll implement fragmentation metrics and validate binpack heuristic changes. Also will test NUMA-aware placement.

jyoti: I'll add region/egress cost into the scorer and run a sensitivity analysis for regulated customers.

samir: Perfect. Let's reconvene after the sim results. Keep notes in the infra runbook under "adaptive-gpu-portfolio" and @samir if you hit blockers. :thumbsup:

maria: quick q — what timeframe for the sim? 14 days of historical spot events ok?

samir: 14 days is good for a start. If we see weekend/week pattern we can extend.

olivia: FYI we should also mock quantized model variants as cheaper fallbacks in the sim. Avoid cold-start if we can switch to a compatible quantized model instead of cross-region spinups.

kevin: noted. I'll add a "compatible-variant" flag in the binpack sim.

infra-bot: [scheduled task] Simulation job queued: infra/sim/adaptive-gpu-portfolio/1795123456

samir: thanks team, will follow up with milestones and a short doc later today.
